findings_to_judge.finding: Kewaunee ran a book-to-bill of roughly 0.83 for all of FY26 -- consolidated backlog fell $214.6m -> $205.0m -> $192.9m -> $183.2m -> $165.9m across five straight quarters (an accelerating burn, -$17.3m in Q4 alone) while quarterly revenue was held flat at $71.1m / $70.1m / $69.4m / $71.4m -- and the FY26 10-K states 'not less than 90% of our order backlog at April 30, 2026 will be shipped during fiscal year 2027', i.e. >=$149m of shipments from backlog against $282m of FY26 revenue; with FY26 opex of $63.7m (~$15.9m/quarter, largely fixed) and a 28.5% gross margin, breakeven revenue is ~$56m per quarter, so Q1 FY27 revenue anywhere in the $55-63m range against the $71.1m year-ago comp puts EPS near zero versus $1.04.

US hot-rolled coil, the primary input to Kewaunee's steel laboratory casework and fume hoods, rose from ~$1,070/short ton at the start of Kewaunee's fiscal Q1 FY27 (SMU average, week of 2026-05-01) to $1,180/st by 2026-08-12, a four-year high with Section 232 at 50% -- a ~10% sequential input-cost step inside a quarter whose revenue is delivered against fixed-price project backlog booked 6-18 months earlier.

On 2026-06-30 CEO Thomas D. Hull III settled 54,388 shares of vesting performance RSUs (which paid out at 150% of target) and elected cash settlement for 17,000 of them at $36.25 rather than taking the stock, with a further 16,243 withheld for tax -- i.e. the CEO converted roughly 60% of a large equity vest away from shares at a price essentially identical to today's $36.01.

Counter-evidence, filed deliberately because it cuts against my main finding: Avantor -- whose VWR arm is the closest public proxy for the US lab distribution channel Kewaunee sells through (two domestic dealers plus a national stocking distributor were 34% of FY26 sales) -- reported on 2026-07-29, after Kewaunee last spoke, that VWR organic growth swung from -4.8% in Q1 to +1.7% in Q2 and raised full-year guidance; Dodge's institutional planning index was also +7.8% year over year in August 2026.
